final_text:
## Incident Report — MTA 2024-07-30 Traffic Analysis Exercise

**Evidence:** `2024-07-30-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (11,562 packets, 585.7 sec, 2024-07-30 06:38:48–06:48:34). No IDS/Suricata alert files were present in the evidence directory; findings are based entirely on packet-level analysis with tshark.

### Victim host

| Attribute | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 | 172.16.1.66 | ARP, all traffic |
| MAC address | 00:1e:64:ec:f3:08 (Intel Corporate) | ARP / Ethernet frames |
| Windows hostname | DESKTOP-SKBR25F | NBNS, Kerberos CNameString, DNS (A record queries for DESKTOP-SKBR25F.wiresharkworkshop.online) |
| Logged-in user | ccollier | Kerberos CNameString field, and confirmed independently inside the malware's own C2 beacon strings |

LAN context: subnet 172.16.1.0/24, gateway 172.16.1.1 (00:15:fa:50:6f:18), domain controller 172.16.1.4 "WIRESHARK-WS-DC" (5c:f9:dd:8c:97:35), AD domain `wiresharkworkshop.online`. All LDAP/Kerberos/SMB/DRSUAPI traffic to 172.16.1.4 is normal domain-joined workstation activity, not malicious.

### Malware family: STRRAT — **signature-confirmed**

Attribution is not inferential. Following TCP stream 83 (172.16.1.66:49754 → 141.98.10.79:12132) shows the malware announcing its own family name in cleartext on every beacon:

```
ping|STRRAT|1BE8292C|DESKTOP-SKBR25F|ccollier|Microsoft Windows 11 Pro|64-bit|Windows Defender|<base64 active-window>|1.6|US:United States|Not Installed|<idle time>
```

This is the documented STRRAT ping/check-in format: a Java-based RAT/credential-stealer known for exactly this pipe-delimited, length-prefixed (`<len>\r\n\r\n<msg>`) heartbeat, its keylogger active-window field (base64-decoded values observed: `Documents`, `Home`, `Pictures`, `Fanad Head Lighthouse - Paint`), and its habit of embedding a build/campaign ID (`1BE8292C` here) and the version string (`1.6`).

### Indicators of Compromise

| Type | Indicator | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| C2 endpoint | **141.98.10.79:12132** | Plaintext TCP, first SYN at t=76.99s, persistent for the remainder of the capture (~508 sec), beaconing every ~5 seconds. No preceding DNS lookup was observed for this IP — the malware connects directly by bare IP, with no supporting domain to report. |
| C2 protocol/campaign ID | `STRRAT` build/campaign tag `1BE8292C`, client version `1.6` | Cleartext in every beacon on stream 83 |
| Victim fingerprinting call | GET `http://ip-api.com/json/` to 208.95.112.1 (frame 9111), immediately after the C2 connection was established (t=77.87s vs C2 SYN at t=76.99s) | HTTP request/response in the capture. This is a legitimate public GeoIP service abused by the malware for self-fingerprinting — report it as a behavioral indicator/context, not as malicious infrastructure in its own right. |
| Compromised host beaconing out | 172.16.1.66 → 141.98.10.79:12132, ~5-second interval, ~137-byte messages containing hostname/user/OS/AV/active-window data | Follow TCP stream 83 |

**No malicious domain, no malicious URL, and no transferred file/SHA256 were observed in this capture.** The only other unusual-looking traffic (bursts to `github.com`/`objects.githubusercontent.com` and `repo1.maven.org` around t=64–68s, and `javadl-esd-secure.oracle.com` at t=340s) presented valid, correctly-matched TLS certificates for their claimed hostnames (GitHub Inc./DigiCert and GlobalSign certs respectively) — there is no domain-fronting or spoofing evidence, and the capture starts mid-session with STRRAT already beaconing, so the initial infection/delivery vector falls outside this capture's time window and cannot be grounded in the traffic. All other DNS/TLS destinations (MSN, Bing, Office, Skype, Windows telemetry, `www.msftconnecttest.com`) are routine Windows/Microsoft background noise and should be treated as benign context, not IOCs.

### Summary

DESKTOP-SKBR25F (172.16.1.66, MAC 00:1e:64:ec:f3:08), logged on as user **ccollier**, is actively compromised with **STRRAT**, a Java-based RAT/credential stealer. It maintains a persistent plaintext C2 channel to **141.98.10.79:12132**, self-identifying with build ID **1BE8292C** and version **1.6**, sending host fingerprint and active-window telemetry every ~5 seconds for the full remainder of the capture. Recommend isolating the host immediately, blocking 141.98.10.79/12132 at the perimeter, and rotating ccollier's credentials given STRRAT's known credential-theft capability.
